task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of June 30, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The Environmental Resources Agency denied Pacific Minerals Corporation's application for a rare earth mining permit at the Granite Ridge deposit in Cascadia County on June 30, 2025.
The agency cited an inadequate plan for managing acid rock drainage, a chemical process in which sulfide minerals exposed during excavation react with water and air to produce sulfuric acid.
Acid drainage from the Granite Ridge ore body, if uncontrolled, could acidify a 38-kilometer stretch of the Coldwater River, which supports a protected steelhead trout population.

ERA director Helen Waters said: "The ore body is economically significant, but the applicant has not demonstrated that it can prevent contamination of the river to a scientifically defensible standard."
Pacific Minerals president Grant Thomas said the company will appeal the decision and submit a revised drainage management plan within 90 days.

The Granite Ridge deposit contains an estimated 480,000 tonnes of rare earth oxides, with concentrations of neodymium and dysprosium used in permanent magnets for electric vehicle motors and wind turbine generators.
The United States currently imports more than 80% of its processed rare earth materials, primarily from China.

ERA's scientific review panel found that Pacific's proposed passive treatment system would be effective for 40 to 60 years but would require perpetual active maintenance after the mine closes — a cost and liability the company has not fully addressed.
Commercial rare earth extraction in the U.S. is currently limited to a single operating site; the Granite Ridge deposit would be the second if permitted.
State legislators from Cascadia County said the denial would cost the region an estimated 1,200 construction jobs and 380 permanent positions.
A coalition of fishing and conservation organizations had argued the proposed drainage plan relied on models calibrated for lower-sulfide ores and was inappropriate for the Granite Ridge formation.
Pacific has been exploring the Granite Ridge site since 2017 and invested approximately $340 million in exploration and permitting activities.
Thomas said the company had offered to post a $120 million environmental performance bond and fund a long-term treatment trust — terms the ERA panel found insufficient.
ERA's decision allows Pacific to reapply within 24 months with a revised environmental management plan.

The critical minerals advisory board had designated rare earth deposits as national priority extraction targets in a 2022 report; that designation does not override environmental permitting authority.
Waters acknowledged the strategic importance of domestic rare earth supply but said the ERA's mandate was environmental protection, not supply chain policy.
A related federal bill that would streamline rare earth permitting on federal lands has passed the Senate but has not advanced in the House.
Environmental review for the original application took 34 months.
Acid rock drainage is a well-documented challenge in mining of sulfide-bearing ores; it has contaminated rivers at multiple historic mining sites in the western United States.
Pacific's stock fell 14% on the day of the decision.

a confirmed environmental impact from current Pacific operations
a country-specific import dependence figure different from 80%
